claims.text: Reconstructed in the Open Air Museum, separate from its ancient sanctuary setting.
Hatshepsut’s red-quartzite bark chapel provided a resting place for Amun’s portable sacred bark. A vestibule and sanctuary form its two-room plan.
Exterior scenes include obelisk erection and the Opet and Beautiful Feast of the Valley processions.
Thutmose III first completed decoration and later dismantled the chapel; Amenhotep III subsequently reused blocks in the Third Pylon foundations. These are separate interventions.

caveats: Present access, exact viewpoints and condition have not been field-verified.
